title: Global module sections on an H1-acyclic qcqs algebraic space
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-scheme, def-trf-algebraic-space], quasi-compact and quasi-separated: its point space is quasi-compact and its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Let $H^q$ mean right-derived global sections of underlying additive sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Suppose $H^1(X,F)=0$ for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module on the small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Put $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and let $p:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ induce the identity on $A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For any $A$-module $M$, let $\widetilde M_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the small etale sheaf associated to the usual quasi-coherent module $\widetilde M$ on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections, def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. Set $M\otimes_A\mathcal O_X=p^*\widetilde M_{\mathrm{et}}$, using tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Then the canonical map $$u_M:M\longrightarrow\Gamma(X,M\otimes_A\mathcal O_X),\qquad m\longmapsto m\otimes1,$$ is an isomorphism of $A$-modules, natural in $A$-linear maps of $M$. Here $u_M$ is the global-section unit for $p^*\dashv p_*$ after the canonical identification $M=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\widetilde M_{\mathrm{et}})$; its local tensor formula is as in [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization]. No finite generation of $M$, Noetherian hypothesis on $X$, or flatness hypothesis on $p$ is assumed. The zero ring, the zero module and the empty space are allowed.

source.place: Tag 07UZ (lemma-vanishing-compute), global-sections assertion under Situation 07UY (situation-vanishing), with the canonical map given by the free-presentation proof.

proof.text: Choose the following explicit free presentation, with small indexing sets in the fixed universe. Let $I$ be the underlying set of $M$, let $F_0=A^{(I)}$, and define $e:F_0\to M$ by $e(e_m)=m$. This is surjective since $m=e(e_m)$. Let $K=\ker(e)$, let $J$ be its underlying set, and define $d:F_1=A^{(J)}\to F_0$ by $d(e_k)=k$. Its image is exactly $K$: every $k\in K$ is an image, and every finite linear combination of such elements lies in $K$. Hence $F_1\xrightarrow d F_0\xrightarrow e M\to0$ is exact. This is a free presentation, not a claim that $d$ is injective.

Put $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $T(N)=p^*\widetilde N_{\mathrm{et}}$. The affine tilde-Gamma adjunction gives that $N\mapsto\widetilde N$ preserves small colimits in all Zariski module sheaves. The Zariski-etale quasi-coherent equivalence carries these to colimits in quasi-coherent etale modules: a map out of a candidate colimit corresponds, under the inverse equivalence, to a compatible family of maps out of the diagram. The kernels-colimits node says that inclusion of quasi-coherent etale modules in all etale modules preserves these colimits, so they are ambient colimits too. Finally $p^*$ is a left adjoint, so preserves small colimits. Thus $T$ preserves direct sums and cokernels. The tilde construction and the Zariski-etale comparison identify $\widetilde A_{\mathrm{et}}$ with $\mathcal O_Y$. For its pullback the chart tensor formula gives $b\otimes a\mapsto b\,p^\sharp(a)$, inverse $b\mapsto b\otimes1$; the balancing relation proves these are inverse. Consequently $T(A)=\mathcal O_X$, $T(A^{(L)})=\mathcal O_X^{(L)}$ for every small set $L$, and $T(F_1)\to T(F_0)\to T(M)\to0$ is exact. Each of these three modules is quasi-coherent: $\mathcal O_X$ has the identity free presentation, and arbitrary sums and cokernels preserve quasi-coherence.

For a small set $L$, the finite subsets $E\subseteq L$, ordered by inclusion, form a small nonempty filtered category: $\varnothing$ is an object and $E\cup E\prime$ dominates any two. The coproduct $\mathcal O_X^{(L)}$ is the filtered colimit of its finite subsums, since compatible maps from all finite subsums are exactly families of maps from its summands. The forgetful functor to abelian sheaves preserves this colimit. Apply the cohomology-filtered-colimit node in degree zero; its hypotheses are exactly the assumed quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $X$. Additivity of global sections identifies the sections of the finite subsum with $A^E$. The same finite-support universal property identifies $\varinjlim_E A^E=A^{(L)}$. We obtain $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X^{(L)})=A^{(L)}$, with the comparison induced by the actual summand injections. Under the identification in step 2, $u_{A^{(L)}}$ sends a basis vector $e_l$ to the section $1$ in the $l$th summand, by the chart-unit formula. Therefore $u_{A^{(L)}}$ is this isomorphism, not merely an abstract module isomorphism.

For any short exact sequence $0\to Q\to P\to R\to0$ of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules, forget the module structure. The forgetful functor is exact, so this is a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves. By the sites-and-cohomology node, the abelian sheaf category has enough injectives, global sections is left exact and additive, and $R^0\Gamma=\Gamma$. The derived-functor long exact sequence therefore gives $0\to\Gamma(Q)\to\Gamma(P)\to\Gamma(R)\to H^1(X,Q)$. Its last term vanishes by hypothesis. Thus $\Gamma(P)\to\Gamma(R)$ is surjective, and global sections is exact on such short exact sequences. All these maps are $A$-linear because they come from module-sheaf morphisms.

Let $B=\operatorname{im}(T(d))=\ker(T(e))$ and $C=\ker(T(F_1)\to B)$. The kernels-colimits node ensures that $B$ and $C$ are quasi-coherent, so step 4 applies to $0\to C\to T(F_1)\to B\to0$ and $0\to B\to T(F_0)\to T(M)\to0$. Hence $\Gamma(T(F_1))\to\Gamma(T(F_0))\to\Gamma(T(M))\to0$ is exact: the first map surjects onto $\Gamma(B)$, which is the kernel of the second. The unit maps give a commuting diagram from the free presentation of step 1 to this row. Indeed, on each local unit tensor a linear map $v:N\to N\prime$ sends $1\otimes n$ to $1\otimes v(n)$ by the chart formula. Step 3 identifies the first two vertical maps with the isomorphisms $u_{F_1}$ and $u_{F_0}$. Thus they identify the images of $d$ and $\Gamma(T(d))$, and induce an isomorphism of the two cokernel quotients. The third vertical map is $u_M$, by commutativity with the surjections from $F_0$, so $u_M$ is an isomorphism.

For every $A$-linear $v:M\to N$, the same local formula gives $\Gamma(T(v))u_M(m)=1\otimes v(m)=u_N(v(m))$. Thus the proved isomorphisms are natural, and they are exactly the specified global-section adjunction units. Their inverses are natural as well by composing this equality with the inverse maps. If $M=0$, both presentation and conclusion are zero. If $X=\varnothing$, then $A=0$ and every unital $A$-module is zero, so the same argument applies. Arbitrary index sets were allowed throughout; neither flatness nor finite generation nor a Noetherian hypothesis was used.

lean.statement: theorem isIso_acyclic_global_module_unit (X : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) [HasSheafify X.etaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u}] [HasExt.{u + 1} (Sheaf X.etaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u})] (hqc : CompactSpace (Point X.obj.obj)) (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated X) (hH : ∀ (F : X.Modules) (_ : F.IsQuasicoherent), Subsingleton (Sheaf.H ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf X.structureSheaf).obj F) 1)) (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (p : X ⟶ schemeSpace (Over.mk (specULiftZIsTerminal.from (Spec A)))) (πA : (Functor.const X.EtaleSiteᵒᵖ).obj A ⟶ X.etaleForget.op ⋙ Scheme.Γ) (hA : IsLimit (Cone.mk A πA)) (hp : ∀ T : X.EtaleSite, πA.app (op T) = (Scheme.ΓSpecIso A).inv ≫ (yoneda.preimage (T.obj.hom ≫ p.hom.hom)).left.appTop) : IsIso (((affineEtaleAssociatedAdjunction A).comp (moduleTensorAdjunction p)).unit)
